rules.title: California — Bereavement Leave (5 days, 5+ employees)

params.covered_relationships: spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, parent-in-law, sibling, grandparent, grandchild

result.summary: Employers with 5 or more employees must give an employee with 30 days of service up to 5 days of bereavement leave per death of a covered family member, taken within 3 months; unpaid unless the employer's policy pays, and the employee may use accrued paid leave. Reproductive loss leave (5 days) added 2024 (Gov. Code 12945.6).

citations.source: Cal. Gov. Code §12945.7
Cal. Gov. Code §12945.6 (reproductive loss)

rules.title: Illinois Family Bereavement Leave Act — 2 weeks (50+ employees)

params.covered_relationships: child, stepchild, spouse, domestic partner, sibling, parent, parent-in-law, grandchild, grandparent, stepparent; pregnancy loss and failed adoption, surrogacy or fertility events

result.summary: FMLA-covered employers (50+) must give eligible employees up to 2 weeks (10 workdays) of unpaid leave per death of a covered family member, taken within 60 days, up to 6 weeks a year for multiple deaths; expanded from child-only bereavement in 2023 and to pregnancy loss events.

citations.source: 820 ILCS 154

rules.title: Illinois Child Extended Bereavement Leave — 12 weeks (250+ employees)

params.covered_relationships: child lost to suicide or homicide

result.summary: Employers with 250 or more full-time employees must give up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave to a parent whose child died by suicide or homicide, taken within one year; may not run concurrently with other leave.

citations.source: 820 ILCS 156 (Child Extended Bereavement Leave Act)

rules.title: Illinois Child Extended Bereavement Leave — 6 weeks (50-249 employees)

params.covered_relationships: child lost to suicide or homicide

result.summary: Employers with 50 to 249 full-time employees must give up to 6 weeks of unpaid leave to a parent whose child died by suicide or homicide.

citations.source: 820 ILCS 156 (Child Extended Bereavement Leave Act)

rules.title: Maryland Flexible Leave Act — Bereavement Use of Accrued Leave (15+ employees)

result.summary: Employers with 15 or more employees that provide paid leave must let employees use it for bereavement of an immediate family member (added 2022); the Act creates no new leave entitlement.

citations.source: Md. Lab. & Empl. §3-802

rules.title: Oregon — OFLA Bereavement Leave (2 weeks, 25+ employees)

params.covered_relationships: spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, parent-in-law, sibling, grandparent, grandchild and their spouses; any individual related by blood or affinity equivalent to family

result.summary: Employers with 25 or more employees must give eligible employees (180 days, average 25 hours a week) up to 2 weeks of unpaid bereavement leave per death, taken within 60 days, up to 4 weeks in a leave year; accrued paid leave may be used.

rules.title: Washington — PFML Bereavement Leave (7 days, death of a child)

params.covered_relationships: a child for whom the employee would have taken bonding leave (birth or placement)

result.summary: Paid Family and Medical Leave: an employee who would have qualified for bonding leave may take up to 7 calendar days of PFML-paid leave after the child's death. Expands on 2026-07-01 to 7 days for the death of any PFML family member (SB 5217).

citations.source: RCW 50A.05.010 (family leave definition)

rules.title: Washington — PFML Bereavement Leave (7 days, any family member)

params.covered_relationships: child, spouse, domestic partner, parent, parent-in-law, sibling, grandparent, grandchild

result.summary: From 2026-07-01 (SB 5217, 2025) PFML bereavement leave covers up to 7 days within 12 months of the death of any qualifying family member, paid through the state PFML program.

citations.source: RCW 50A.05.010 as amended by SB 5217 (2025)
